props.gloss_en: one who takes the mother with the young -- R' Yehuda: he is flogged and does not send
and the Sages: he sends and is not flogged
this is the rule: any prohibition that has in it [a command to] arise and do -- one is not flogged for it
horn 1: R' Yehuda's reason [for lashes] is that he holds one is flogged for a prohibition converted to a positive command
horn 2: in general he holds one is not flogged for a prohibition converted to a positive command, and here the reason is that he holds 'shaleach' means from the outset
the baraita: a thief and a robber are included in lashes -- the words of R' Yehuda
yet here it is a prohibition converted to a positive command, for the Merciful One said 'you shall not rob' and 'he shall restore the robbed item'
R' Zeira: any baraita not taught in the houses of R' Chiyya and R' Oshaya is corrupt, and you may not object from it in the study hall
the baraita of R' Oshaya and R' Chiyya: 'do not return' and he returned, 'do not finish' and he finished -- included in forty lashes, the words of R' Yehuda
the baraita: 'leave nothing of it until morning... burn in fire' -- the verse gives a positive command after the prohibition to tell you one is not flogged for it, the words of R' Yehuda
how far does he send it? Rav Yehuda: enough that it leaves his hand
by what does he send it? Rav Huna: by its legs
Rav Yehuda: by its wings
Rav Huna's ground: 'that send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey' (Isa 32:20)
Rav Yehuda's ground: for those are its legs [the wings are what it goes by]
a man clipped its wings, sent it and afterwards caught it -- Rav Yehuda had him flogged
and said to him: go, let its wings grow, and send it
actually [Rav Yehuda acted] according to the Rabbis
and [the lashes were] rabbinic lashes of rebelliousness
the man: the teima [bird] -- what is it [as to sending]?
Rava: does this man not know that a kosher bird must be sent?
the mishna: if there is only one chick or one egg -- he must send
he sent it, and Rava surrounded it with nets and caught it
the baraita: dovecote pigeons and attic pigeons are obligated in sending
and they are forbidden on account of robbery because of the ways of peace
R' Yosei bar R' Chanina: a man's courtyard acquires for him without his knowledge
read here 'if [a nest] happens before you' -- excluding the readily available
Rabba: an egg -- it is with the emergence of its majority that [one] becomes obligated in sending
it is not acquired until it falls into his courtyard
and when it teaches 'obligated in sending' -- [it means] before it falls into his courtyard
[the robbery clause is] about their mothers
or say: actually about the egg, and once an egg's majority has emerged, his mind is on it
Rav: one may not acquire eggs on which the mother is resting
as it says 'send the mother' and only then 'the young you may take' (Deut 22:7)
you may even say: [the baraita holds] even though it fell into his courtyard
wherever he can acquire, his courtyard acquires too; wherever he cannot acquire, his courtyard does not acquire for him either
[the 'ways of peace' clause is] about a minor
this is what it says: the minor's father must return it to him, because of the ways of peace
Levi bar Simon transferred the produce of his dovecote to Rav Yehuda
Shmuel: go bang on the nest so they rise, and acquire them
that was new produce, which Levi bar Simon himself had not acquired
and this is what he said to him: bang on the nest so they rise and Levi bar Simon acquires them, then let him transfer them to you by a cloth
